Time_Annotation: Amanda originated as a tropical wave that moved into the eastern Pacific on May 16. It continued west, organizing into a tropical depression around 18:00 UTC on May 22 and further intensifying into a tropical storm a day later. After attaining hurricane strength at 12:00 UTC on May 24, the storm began a period of rapid intensification, peaking as a high-end Category 4 hurricane with winds of 155 mph (250 km/h) within 24 hours. The hurricane fell to tropical storm strength early on May 28, weakened to tropical depression strength early on May 29, and dissipated around 18:00 UTC that day.
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: A river near Coyuca de Benítez overflowed its banks. Three trees were brought down and a vehicle in Acapulco was destroyed, near where one person was killed. In Colima, minor landslides occurred, resulting in the closure of Federal Highway 200. Two people perished in Michoacán while several roads were destroyed in Zitácuaro.
Main_Event_Annotation: After attaining hurricane strength at 12:00 UTC on May 24, the storm rapidly intensified and peaked as a high-end Category 4 hurricane, making Amanda the strongest May tropical cyclone on record in the basin.
Hazards_Annotation: The report mentions winds of 155 mph (250 km/h) indicating significant wind hazards, and it also notes that a river near Coyuca de Benítez overflowed its banks, causing flooding.

Canada is cited when a peak gust was recorded as the storm moved across Lake Superior toward Northern Ontario and when the extratropical cyclone reached James Bay and later Labrador.

Time_Annotation: A tropical disturbance formed along the near equatorial trough on April 20 well to the south of Guam. The system slowly increased in organization, becoming a tropical depression on April 26. The system quickly developed thereafter, becoming a typhoon on April 27 while moving northward. The system reached its peak intensity on April 28. South-westerly vertical wind shear led to a weakening trend to begin on April 29. On April 30, Ken's low level circulation was exposed, no longer having any thunderstorms near the center. The remnant low drifted westward, dissipating by May 3.

Time_Annotation: An extratropical disturbance formed east of Madagascar on January 11, and transitioned into a subtropical depression the next day. On January 16, the last advisory was issued for Dando as the system weakened to a remnant low. After making landfall on January 17, the remnants of Dando moved inland before dissipating on January 18.
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: Dando was noted as the first storm since Tropical Storm Domoina in 1984 to hit southern Mozambique. Main_Event_Annotation: The article describes the system as retaining subtropical characteristics as it moved toward the African mainland and notes that by January 15 it reached the equivalent of cyclone strength and was allocated the name Dando by NWS Madagascar.
Hazards_Annotation: Heavy rains triggered significant flooding in southern Mozambique, with flash floods washing away bridges and damaging roads and buildings, while along the coast waves up to 6 m prevented fishermen from leaving port, indicating hazards of both flood and high winds.

Time_Annotation: Morakot spawned from an area of disturbed weather in the Philippine Sea on July 31.[16] It made landfall on southern Taiwan on August 3 and then its final landfall near Quanzhou, China the next day, before dissipating several hours after landfall.[13]
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: In Taiwan, where Morakot first made landfall, heavy rainfall resulted in flooding.[16] In China, record rainfall was reported with significant impacts in Quanzhou, including widespread power outages and economic losses.[13]

Time_Annotation: On October 21, the JMA started to monitor a tropical depression near Palau.[439] By the next day the PAGASA started to monitor the tropical depression and named it Ofel.[440] Late on October 23, the JMA upgraded the tropical depression to a tropical storm, naming it Son-Tinh.[441] On October 25, Son-Tinh strengthened into a severe tropical storm.[444] Son-Tinh reached typhoon strength on October 27.[445] Late on October 27, the system rapidly strengthened into a category 3 typhoon in just 6 hours.[446]
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: The article mentions that the system made landfall over Leyte and traversed the Philippines, and later states that it affected Vietnam and Hainan Island.[442][443][447]
Main_Event_Annotation: The report details that the tropical depression was upgraded to a tropical storm (and later reached typhoon strength), which aligns with a Tropical Storm/Cyclone event.[441][445]
Hazards_Annotation: The text describes widespread flooding in the Philippines, including rivers bursting their banks, as well as strong winds that derailed a train in Quezon.[450]

Hazards_Annotation: Hazard details include maximum sustained winds of 150 km/h (90 mph) and gusts exceeding 215 km/h (130 mph) as stated by the Central Meteorological Observatory, as well as winds up to Force 10 affecting parts of the Aleutians.

Time_Annotation: A low-level circulation north of Chuuk organized into a tropical depression on August 4. The depression stalled on August 5 and August 6, allowing it to strengthen into a tropical storm and mature into a typhoon on August 7. The typhoon turned northward and rapidly intensified to maximum sustained winds of 130 knots (240 km/h) on August 8, and as a 35-knot tropical storm, it hit North Korea on August 14.

Hazards_Annotation: The typhoon produced maximum sustained winds of 130 knots indicating wind hazards, while heavy rains led to flash flooding, landslides, and mudslides, confirming flood hazards.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Making its way toward Tupelo, the massive tornado killed a family of 13 as their house was swept away.
Retroactively rated F5, the tornado caused total destruction along its path through the Willis Heights neighborhood – dozens of large and well built mansions were swept completely away in this area.
Although missing the business district, the tornado moved through the residential areas of north Tupelo, destroying many homes, and killing whole families.
The Gum Pond area of Tupelo was the worst hit – homes along the pond were swept into the water with their victims.
The tornado destroyed the water tower and produced numerous fires in its wake.
As the tornado exited the city's east side, the large concrete Battle of Tupelo monument was toppled to the ground and destroyed.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: On April 23, an F2 tornado northeast of Weleetka, Oklahoma overturned a school bus several times, demolished several other buildings on a dairy farm and destroyed 25 telephone poles.

The worst tornado was a small, but deadly F2 tornado that moved northeastward and hit Eagletown, Oklahoma, destroying three homes, damaging six others, killing one person, and injuring 14 others.
An F2 tornado skipped northeastward through the college section of Texarkana, Arkansas, causing considerable damage to homes, trees, and vehicles, although there were no casualties.

Another long-tracked F2 tornado touched down in Fayette, Mississippi and struck Downtown Jackson along its 96.7-mile-path (155.6 km). Although there were no casualties reported, several homes, other buildings, and trees were damaged and outbuildings were destroyed or damaged.

The first fatal tornado of June 8 was an F4 tornado that struck Temperance, Michigan before moving through areas south of Erie, killing four and injuring 17.

The only Ohio tornado of June 8 became a long‐tracked F4 tornado family that struck the cities of Fremont, Sandusky, Elyria, and Western Cleveland, causing catastrophic damage, killing 17 and injuring 379.

Locations: between Sharon Hollow and Ann Arbor

In the community of Beecher, part of the northern suburbs of Flint, Michigan, a deadly tornado swept through—113 people lost their lives in the town alone, and the tornado killed a total of 116 people while injuring 844 others.
In all, 12 tornadoes touched down on June 8, killing 142 people and injuring 1,293 others.
A violent F4 tornado struck Worcester, Massachusetts with no warning; the hardest hit area was Assumption College and its surrounding neighborhoods, where 42 people were killed.
By the end of the June 9 event, the tornadoes in New Hampshire and Massachusetts killed 94 people (noting an earlier count of 94 dead and 1,228 injured before final tallies were reported).

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: On October 11, a depression named Maymay by the PAGASA formed off the coast of the Philippines. Despite being short-lived and dissipating the next day, two people were killed from the storm.

On October 13, a tropical depression formed west of the Philippines in the South China Sea, reached tropical storm status as Sonca, made landfall in Quang Ngai Province, Vietnam, and dissipated shortly after; 10 fatalities were reported due to heavy precipitation from the storm.

On October 18, a tropical depression south of Okinawa, classified as 25W, dissipated in the South China Sea without intensifying further; however, two reported deaths were recorded in the Philippines.

On October 26, a tropical depression formed in the Philippine Sea and evolved into Tropical Storm Nalgae (Paeng), making five landfalls across the Philippine archipelago and later striking over Xiangzhou District, Zhuhai. Nalgae caused heavy damage and flooding across the Philippines and killed at least 154 people in the country.

On December 9, a tropical depression formed east of the Philippines and was named Pakhar (also known as Rosal by PAGASA). As it approached, warnings were raised in Southern Luzon, and Pakhar killed 8 people indirectly from a flood that swept away a jeep in Rizal.

Time_Annotation: Hurricane hunters investigated the depression on the morning of June 2, and determined that it had strengthened into Tropical Storm Arlene.[65] At 06:00 UTC on June 3, it weakened to a tropical depression, six hours before degenerating into a remnant low about 220 mi (355 km) west of Key West, Florida.
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: Arlene brought 2–6 in (51–152 mm) of rainfall to many locations in Central and South Florida,[66] and the remnants of Arlene also dropped rainfall on several islands in the Bahamas, peaking at 8.5 in (220 mm) of precipitation in Cockburn Town.[67]

Hazards_Annotation: The remnants of Arlene generated severe thunderstorms across Southern Florida with wind gusts up to 83 mph (134 km/h) at the Fort Lauderdale–Hollywood International Airport,[68] and Arlene brought heavy rainfall (2–6 in, with a peak of 9.82 in in Lakeland)[66][67] which is consistent with flooding hazards for a Tropical Storm/Cyclone.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The tornado rapidly intensified to low-end EF4 strength as it entered the city of Washington, leveling and partially sweeping away a couple of homes along English Oak St in the Woodridge Trace subdivision at 170 mph (270 km/h).

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: 16 apartment buildings and a nearby restaurant
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: The tornado intensified further to mid-range EF4 strength as it struck the Georgetown Commons apartment complex along Georgetown Road; the top two stories were destroyed, and nearby apartment buildings suffered major roof damage. A truck in the parking lot was lifted and wrapped violently around a tree. The sixteen apartment buildings and a nearby restaurant that also sustained heavy damage were torn down.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: a building on the course property was leveled
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Now moving at 65 mph, the tornado directly hit the Hillcrest Golf Course, which was closed for two years following the tornado. A building on the course property was leveled as the tornado shredded trees and tore off the carpeting on the minigolf course.

The tornado crossed Washington Road into Washington Estates, sustaining estimated wind speeds of 180 mph (290 km/h). An Advance Auto Parts store alongside Washington Road was leveled by the tornado; multiple employees were inside when the building was flattened, but no one was injured.
On Fayette Avenue, the tornado caused destructive damage to numerous homes at EF4 intensity, killing an 82-year-old woman who initially survived but died from her injuries a week later.
The tornado slightly weakened to low-end EF4 strength alongside Elgin Avenue; some homes on Flossmoor Avenue were swept away.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: a row of well-constructed homes and another home
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: On the Trail Edge subdivision, the tornado abruptly intensified to high-end EF4 strength with estimated wind speeds up to 190 mph (310 km/h). The most violent damage to occur from the tornado happened alongside Mackenzie Street, where a row of well-constructed homes was completely obliterated and all debris was swept away, leaving only bare foundations; along Bishops Court, another home was demolished and had all debris swept clean from the foundation and wind-rowed.

On Kingsbury Road, Our Savior Lutheran Church received considerable damage. All the windows were blown out, and the roof sustained moderate damage; the doors to the walkout basement were ripped away, and the church's garage was demolished.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: another row of homes on Coventry Drive; four rows of homes on Holborn Court; another row of homes on Westminster Drive
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Entering Devonshire Estates, the tornado maintained high-end EF4 intensity, leveling or sweeping away another row of homes on Coventry Drive while traveling northeast at around 65 mph (105 km/h). Four rows of homes on Holborn Court were leveled; debris was partially swept off of their foundations. Along Westminster Drive, another row of homes was leveled and either partially swept away or completely swept away from their foundations, and trees were shredded and debarked.
A farmstead on N Main Street was destroyed, and debris was partially swept off its foundation.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Num: an entire farmstead destroyed; farmhouse leveled and outbuildings destroyed
Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Still maintaining 190-mile-per-hour winds, the tornado crossed Duluth Lane, where an entire farmstead was destroyed: the farmhouse was leveled and swept away, some outbuildings on the farmstead were destroyed and reduced down to their foundations, and some grain bins lost their tops.

Two homes north of Roanoke sustained substantial damage; one lost its exterior walls (destroyed at near EF3 intensity) while the other lost most of its roof.
On Illinois 117 northwest of Benson, a farmhouse lost its exterior walls as the tornado restrengthened to EF3 intensity.
As the tornado traveled further northeast, a home was shifted off of its foundation at high-end EF2 intensity.
A well-built home had its roof ripped off on County Road 2300.
A poorly constructed home was swept away as the tornado approached I-39 and crossed Illinois 117.
Just before the tornado left Woodford county, a home lost its roof and its wall partially collapsed as the tornado slightly weakened.
The tornado maintained EF2 intensity as it stripped away a large portion of a home's roof along E 7th Road.
Small outbuildings were destroyed along E 7th Road.
0.5 miles (0.80 km) west of Dana, a machinery shed was destroyed as the tornado weakened to EF1 strength.
South of Long Point, the tornado restrengthened back to EF2 intensity, demolishing several outbuildings.
A large shed containing a fire engine was destroyed, with the fire engine tipping onto its side.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: An intense linear mesoscale convective system formed during the overnight hours of July 28 into the early morning hours of July 29, producing widespread damaging winds across Wisconsin before moving south into northern Illinois and Indiana. Countless trees and power lines were downed, structures were damaged, and more than 130,000 homes and businesses were without power in Wisconsin and Illinois following the passage of the damaging line of storms.
Two of these tornadoes caused EF1 damage in the Madison suburbs of West Middleton and Verona.
An EF1 tornado also caused considerable damage to homes, trees, and power poles in and around the small community of Concord.
Two other EF1 tornadoes occurred near Dousman, where docks and boats were damaged at a small lake, and trees and homes were damaged as well.
Some of the tornadoes were strong and damaging, including an EF2 tornado that caused heavy damage to homes, outbuildings, power poles, and trees in New Athens, Ohio.
Another EF2 tornado destroyed a metal shed, caused major tree damage, and completely deforested a wooded hillside near Salineville.
In Wintersville, an EF1 tornado damaged a church, one business, and 23 homes.
In the Philadelphia suburbs, a destructive low-end EF3 tornado struck Trevose and Bensalem, Pennsylvania, causing major damage to multiple car dealership buildings and a mobile home park.
An anticyclonic EF0 tornado also briefly touched down in the Philadelphia neighborhood of Bustleton, causing minor damage to trees, an apartment building, and a few other structures.
A damaging EF2 tornado moved through High Bar Harbor, New Jersey, later that night, tearing the roofs off of multiple homes, tossing boats and a boat trailer, snapping many trees and power poles.

Many trees and power poles were snapped by the Wuhan tornado as well.

The narrow but strong tornado downed power lines, snapped or uprooted large trees, and damaged multiple homes and apartment buildings, some of which sustained shattered windows and had roofing torn off. Brick fencing was blown over, and projectiles were driven into the exterior walls of structures as well.

A high-end EF2 tornado also touched down in a rural area outside of Jinzhou, knocking down metal truss electrical transmission towers, and snapping or uprooting many hardwood trees, a few of which sustained some low-end debarking. Power poles were snapped, vehicles were damaged, and a brick outbuilding was destroyed. Farm fields were also scoured by the tornado.

Total_Summary_Buildings_Damaged.Total_Buildings_Damaged_Annotation: Many residential dwellings were damaged, some estimates suggest around 2,000, primarily due to overloaded guttering causing roofing leaks and collapses; others were damaged due to flooding, water damage, hail window damage and wind damage.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Several major buildings in the city were damaged and evacuated, including Southern Cross station, evacuated primarily due to a roofing collapse; and Flinders Street station, evacuated primarily due to flooding. The Highpoint Shopping Centre, Chadstone Shopping Centre and The Jam Factory were also evacuated. Docklands Stadium was evacuated when roofing at Gate 3 collapsed. Media House and the ABC Headquarters in Southbank were also damaged with roofing collapses. The Melbourne Theatre Company's new building was inundated with water, resulting in the cancellation of several performances for the days following. Neighbouring Melbourne Recital Centre also suffered damage with flooding of internal spaces and hail damage to windows and signage. The roof of The Arts Centre was badly hit, with Premier John Brumby stating that to repair 'The damage bill will clearly run to the hundreds of thousands if not millions of dollars'. Crown Casino was severely affected with its Village Cinema being closed as a result of flooding as well as banks of gaming tables and machines being cordoned off due to leaks.

Hazards_Annotation: The article mentions that 'four of the named storms attained maximum sustained winds of at least 120 km/h (75 mph)', which indicates wind as the primary hazard associated with tropical cyclones.

Specific_Instance_Per_Administrative_Are.Annotation: Continuing northeastward into the Old Kingston community, the tornado rapidly intensified to EF3 strength as it crossed County Road 43. Several mobile homes were obliterated and swept away, with debris being scattered long distances across fields.
The tornado briefly weakened to EF1 strength as it crossed the Coosa River before reaching EF2 intensity again north of Titus, snapping countless pine trees and unroofing another home.

As the tornado widened and intensified along County Roads 14 and 18 northwest of Equality, several vehicles were moved or flipped, numerous trees were snapped, and a few site-built homes sustained major structural damage, including a poorly anchored house that was completely leveled.
The tornado quickly narrowed and weakened back to EF1 intensity as it crossed over SR 9 to the north of Equality, where a mobile home and a site-built home suffered roof damage.

Re-strengthening to EF2 intensity as it crossed the Tallapoosa River along the north side of Lake Martin near the US 280 bridge, the tornado damaged many homes (with roofs ripped off or partial wall loss) and also destroyed boat houses.

Time_Annotation: On the evening of December 16, the JTWC issued a Tropical Cyclone Formation alert... Hazards_Annotation: Based on its classification as a Tropical Storm/Cyclone (per the Main_Event--Hazard association table), Severe Tropical Storm Cinda is linked with hazards such as wind, flood, and lightning.

Time_Annotation: After weakening slightly early on January 10, Dongo began to turn towards the southeast. Six hours later, however, Dongo intensified into a severe tropical storm while reaching its peak intensity with winds of 95 km/h (60 mph 10-minute winds). Despite moving over cooler waters, the storm remained a severe tropical storm until being declared extratropical at 0600 UTC on January 12.
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: At 06:00 UTC, MFR designated the system as a Zone of Disturbed Weather 1,530 km (950 mi) northeast of Mauritius, and later Dongo was noted to peak about 1,240 km (770 mi) east-southeast of Mauritius.
Main_Event_Annotation: The system was first upgraded to Moderate Tropical Storm Dongo and later intensified into a severe tropical storm, indicating it falls under the Tropical Storm/Cyclone category.
Hazards_Annotation: The report highlights peak wind speeds (95 km/h and 100 km/h) as key characteristics, which aligns with Wind being the primary hazard for a Tropical Storm/Cyclone.
